Byte 2: waveform (high nibble) and pulse width high (low nibble).
Byte 3: pulse width low. The pulse width bytes are inverted.
Byte 4: effect speed. Byte 5: effect flags.
Bytes 6-11: value and length of the 3 effect phases.
Flag bit 1: sets the sync bit.
Flag bit 2: sets triangle with ring modulation ($14).
Command $f4 a b: note length = duration a + duration b (low nibbles, table at $9ed1).
Command $f5 n: the voice continues with tune n from its start. Clears the filter routing bit of the voice.
Clears the resonance and the filter bit of the voice.
Command $f6 n: sets CIA 1 timer B (the music tick rate) to entry n of the tempo table at $9ef1.
Command $f7 n: plays tune n on the voice, then returns after this command (see cmd_return).
Returns with X = music_voice * 2.
Command $f8: returns to the tune and read offset that cmd_call_tune saved.
Command $f9 n: loads filter setting n (11 bytes, pointer table at $9f37) and starts the filter on this voice.
Byte 0: sweep speed. Bytes 1-2: start cutoff (high, low).
Byte 3: resonance and routing, with the bit of this voice.
Byte 4: filter mode. Clears the voice 3 off bit.
Bytes 5-10: step (times 8) and length of the 3 sweep phases.
Adds A to the read offset of voice music_voice. Returns X = music_voice * 2.
Decrements the note time of each voice. At 0, clears the gate. Also decrements the fade delay.
Clears the gate and the test bit of the voice.
Does one step of the effects of each voice: pitch steps, pulse sweep and frequency slide, in 3 phases.
Bit 7 clear: the effects of the voice are off.
Waits until the effect delay is 0.
Length 0, or all steps done: goes to the next phase.
Goes to the next of the 3 phases. After phase 2, loops only when flag bit 3 is set.
Flag bit 6: adds the step value to the pitch of voice X and sets the frequency from the table at $9d51.
Keeps the pitch below $c0.
Flag bit 5: adds the step value times 16 to the pulse width of voice X.
Flag bit 4: adds the step value to the frequency of voice X. Bit 7 of the phase length makes the step negative.
Does one step of the filter sweep: adds the step of the phase to the cutoff, in 3 phases.
Speed 0: no sweep.
After phase 2, the sweep starts again only when the step of phase 1 is not 0.
Adds the step of the filter phase to the 11-bit cutoff, then sets the cutoff.
Writes the 11-bit cutoff filter_cutoff to the SID shadow (low 3 bits, high 8 bits).
Starts the tune that sound_request,x asks for on voice X. When sound is off, drops requests of $83 and higher.
Starts the tune that sound_request,x asks for on voice X. In music mode (sound_off bit 7 set), drops the effect requests $83 and higher.
Stops the effects, the note time and the filter sweep. Read offset = 0.
Clears the resonance and the filter bit of the voice.
Fades the master volume in (to 15) or out (to 0), one step after each fade delay.
Silences the SID. Clears the SID shadow, the driver workspace $0200-$0259 and the driver variables $ce-$ed.
32 bytes: the last byte $ed is after freq_slide_step_hi, and nothing uses it.
Copies the SID shadow ($31-$49) to the SID registers $d400-$d418.
Effects tick on CIA 1 timer A. Updates the effects and the filter sweep, then writes the SID.
Does nothing while the music tick runs.
SID frequency of each quarter tone: 192 words, low byte first, 24 steps for each octave. Note byte n uses entry 2n. The driver adds the base $9d51 as two immediates at $9828 and $9bb5.

SID frequencies, 192 words, low byte first. Even entry 2n: the NTSC frequency of semitone n from C0. Odd entries: the mean of the two neighbours. The last entry is $ffff. Valid notes are $00-$5f. The tunes use notes $01-$54. The driver adds the base $9d51 as two immediates at $9828 and $9bb5.
Note lengths in music ticks, 16 words. Event bytes $c0-$cf select entry 0-15. Command $f4 adds two entries.
Note lengths in music ticks, 16 words. Event bytes $c0-$cf select entry 0-15. Command $f4 adds two entries. No tune uses entries 12-15.
CIA 1 timer B values for command $f6 (tempo), 17 words. A larger value gives a slower tune.

CIA 1 timer B values for command $f6 (tempo), 17 words: 1000000 / rate, for 16-80 music ticks per second at 1 MHz. The PAL clock makes each rate 1.5% slower. A larger value gives a slower tune. The tunes use only entries 10-16.
Offset of the SID registers of voice 0, 1 and 2 (0, 7, 14) in the SID copy at $31.
Offset of voice 0, 1 and 2 in the effect phase tables at $0200 and $0209 (3 phases each).
The command bytes $f0-$f9 of the tune data. The driver compares an event byte with each entry.
Handler of each command $f0-$f9: rest, restart, end, instrument, length, goto, tempo, call, return, filter.
Pointers to the 16 filter settings of command $f9.
Pointers to the 16 filter settings of command $f9. No tune uses settings 0 and 9.
Filter setting, 11 bytes. Bytes 0-4: step delay, cutoff high, cutoff low, resonance and routing, mode. Then 3 phases: cutoff step (x 8), step count.
Start of each tune, 114 words (tunes $00-$71). The sound request $80+n in $dc-$de starts tune n.

Start of each tune, 114 words (tunes $00-$71). The sound request $80+n in $dc-$de starts tune n. Tunes $58, $59 and $65-$68 hold only the end command $f2. No request, goto or call starts tunes $58, $59, $60, $65-$68 and $6f-$71.
Tune data: bytes $00-$bf are notes, $c0-$cf select a note length, $f0-$f9 are commands with 0-2 argument bytes.

Instruments of command $f3, 12 bytes each (63 entries). Command $f3 n reads entry n at $a21a+12n. Bytes 0-3: attack/decay, sustain/release, waveform with inverted pulse width high, inverted pulse width low. Bytes 4-5: effect delay, effect flags. Then 3 phases: value, length.

Instruments of command $f3, 12 bytes each (63 entries). Command $f3 n reads entry n at $a21a+12n. Bytes 0-3: attack/decay, sustain/release, waveform with inverted pulse width high, inverted pulse width low. Bytes 4-5: effect delay, effect flags. Then 3 phases: value, length. No tune uses instruments $2f, $30, $36, $38 and $39.

Work bitmap of the fight area: 8 character rows of 320 bytes (bitmap rows 14-21). The fighters are drawn here. The arena change at $8d07 also uses $a50e-$b50d as 16 rows of 256 bytes and swaps it with $d000-$dfff.
Columns 4-35 of each work bitmap row start at $a52e+320k (256 bytes). $8b41 copies them to the screen bitmap.
Columns 4-35 of bitmap row 14+k, at $af2e+320k. $8ad5 fills them, $8b0b copies them to the work bitmap.
End of the clean copy of the fight area: rows of 320 bytes from $af0e. $ae96-$b27d is not in the program.
End of the clean copy of the fight area: rows of 320 bytes from $af0e. $b000-$b3e7 is not in the program.
Pointers to the 24 texts. The text printer at $9173 draws text $80+n from entry n.

Text format: column, row, colour byte, then characters. $0d starts a new line with 3 new header bytes. The colour byte goes to screen RAM (high nibble) and colour RAM (low nibble). Other characters than A-Z and text_special_chars end the text. Text 0: "000" at row 22. No code prints text 0.
Text 1: the version "V 05 05 87". CTRL+V shows it.
Texts 2-4: "1PLR", "2PLR" and "DEMO" at row 24.
Text 5: "PAUSED". No code prints text 5.
Text 6: two digits at row 5. $828e writes the time ($c8) or the level ($be) into them.
Texts 7 and 8: the 5-digit scores of fighter 0 and 1 at row 5.
Text 9: "YOUR END HAS COME". The final stage of part 2 prints it. No code of part 1 prints it.
Text 10: "THANKS BIG BOY". The final stage of part 2 prints it. No code of part 1 prints it.
Texts 11-23: the energy display for energy 0-12, 20 bytes each. Each has 2 lines of 6 characters. "(" and ")" draw the energy units. $82d4 writes the column of the fighter into byte 0 and byte 10.
The 13 characters other than A-Z that the text printer draws: 0-9, space, "(" and ")".
Font glyph of each character in text_special_chars.
Column of the energy display of fighter 0 and 1 (0 and 34).
Five score digits (00010) that $83a3 adds to the score for each unit of time that remains.
Pointers to the 4 corner animations. $81b8 plays animation n when $5b,x holds $80+n.

Corner animation: column, row, width and height in cells, then frame addresses. A word below 4 is a command. Commands: 0 restarts, 1 jumps to the offset that follows, 2 starts the animation that follows, 3 stops.
Pointers to the pose sequence of each move $00-$1d. The move number is in $67,x (bit 7 set).

Move sequence: pose numbers, then $ff and a command. 0 loops, 1 sets the move to 1, 2 jumps to the offset that follows. Command 3 starts the move that follows (move $9d also turns the fighter). Other commands hold the last pose.

Move sequence: pose numbers, then $ff and a command. 0 loops, 1 sets the move to 1, 2 jumps to the offset that follows. Command 3 starts the move that follows (move $9d also turns the fighter). Other commands hold the last pose. No sequence uses commands 1 and 2.
Move $15: no code and no table starts it. Its pose $3e uses the record of pose $0d.
Moves of fighter 1 ($68) that make $87ce update fighter 0 first. Else it updates fighter 1 first.
Moves that $84b0 and $8556 do not change. $84b0 reads no joystick and $8556 does not start move $1a.
Pointers to the pose records of poses $00-$5a. The pose number is in $6f,x.

Pose record: 9 sprite part numbers (3 x 3 grid), move flags, step size, sprite count. Part n is at $0800+64n, 0 is empty. Move flag bits 3 and 4 move the fighter by the step size. 4 bytes follow for each sprite. Sprite bytes: pointer minus $20, colour (bit 7 set: multicolour, else fighter_colours), Y position, X offset.
The 12 poses that can hit. $86b9 finds the pose of the attacker here. Entry n selects hit list n.
Pointers to the hit list of each attack pose.
Hit list: pairs of defender pose and hit record number. $ff ends the list.
Lists 8-10 (attack poses $24-$26 of move $91) use only records $11 and $12: the defender gets move $99, without damage or score.

Hit records, 4 bytes each (39 records). $86c6 reads record n at $c642+4n. Byte 0: distance mask (ANDed with bit_masks of the distance). Byte 1: new move of the defender, 0 for none. Byte 2: hit_sounds entry (high nibble), energy loss when not 0 (low nibble). Byte 3: hit_sprite_effects entry (high nibble), score_values entry (low nibble). 0 selects none.

Hit records, 4 bytes each (39 records). $86c6 reads record n at $c642+4n. Byte 0: distance mask (ANDed with bit_masks of the distance). Byte 1: new move of the defender, 0 for none. Byte 2: hit_sounds entry (high nibble), energy loss when not 0 (low nibble). Byte 3: hit_sprite_effects entry (high nibble), score_values entry (low nibble). 0 selects none. A low nibble not 0 in byte 2 takes 1 energy unit (one DEC). The masks use only bits 0-3, so only distances 0-3 hit. No hit list uses records 1, 7 and 9.
Sound requests for $dc, $dd and $de, 3 bytes each (5 entries). A zero byte leaves that request.
Hit sprite effects, 3 bytes each: sprite animation, Y position, X offset. Entry 0 is not used.
Score values, 5 digits each: 0, 500, 200, 100, 50. Entry 0 is not used.
Moves that play a sound at one step of their sequence (7 entries).
Sequence step ($69,x) of each entry of swing_sound_moves.
Sound request for $dc and $dd of each entry of swing_sound_moves.
Colour of the hires fighter sprites for each level in $be (8 entries).
Pointers to the AI column table of each level in $be (8 entries).
AI column tables, 32 bytes each. A random number (0-31) selects a column (0-7) of the AI joystick row.
Distance band (0-7) for each distance between the fighters in $aa (0-39).
Pointers to the AI row of each pose $00-$5a of the other fighter.
AI rows, 8 bytes each: one byte for each distance band. The byte selects an AI joystick row.
Row list $0a: no entry of ai_row_ptrs points to this row.
No entry of ai_row_ptrs points to this row.
AI joystick rows, 8 bytes each (22 rows). $85a0 reads row n at $c9ce+8n. Each byte is a joystick value: bits 0-3 up, down, left, right, bit 4 fire.
Row $04. Row $08 has the same 8 bytes.
Row $08: the same bytes as row $04.
Pointers to the sprite animations $00-$15. The animation number is in $0292,x (bit 7 set).

Sprite animation: frame time, colour and flags, then sprite pointers minus $20. Flag bits: 7 multicolour, 6 wide, 5 tall. $ff and a command end it. 0 loops, 1 stops the sprite, 2 jumps to the offset that follows. 3 starts the animation that follows.
A copy of sprite_anim_04. No pointer points here.
Pointers to the 4 sprite set-ups that $8cab selects with $cb. Nothing calls $8cab in part 1, so these set-ups stay unused.
Sprite set-up, 12 bytes: animations of sprites 3-0, X positions of sprites 3-0, Y positions minus $a2.
Start motion of the goblin (sprite 4) in the final stage of part 2. Part 1 has no final stage: no code reads it.
Start motion of the bolt (sprite 4) in the final stage of part 2: $8a or $8b, by a random bit. Part 1 has no final stage: no code reads it.
Pointers to a list of 4 moves for each goblin motion. One of these moves of fighter 0 removes the goblin. No code of part 1 reads them.
Pointers to a list of 4 moves for each bolt motion. In part 2, fighter 0 survives the bolt when it does one of these moves. No code of part 1 reads them.
Pointers to the sprite motions $00-$0b. The motion number is in $025a,x (bit 7 set).

Sprite motion: steps of 4 bytes. Directions (bit 0 up, 1 down, 2 left, 3 right), speeds (high nibble X, low nibble Y), frames, command. Commands: 0 next step, 1 new motion and animation follow, 2 new motion follows, 3 step follows, 4 stops. Other values: a sound request follows.
X offset of sprites 0-2 from the fighter for each facing. $8f97 uses it for move $88.
Animation of sprite 0 for each facing ($8f97). The 2 bytes after it are not used.
Animations of sprites 1 and 0 that $9517 starts.
Animations of sprites 4 and 3 that $9577 starts.
Motion of sprite 0 for each facing ($8f97).
Motion of sprite 1 for each facing ($8f97).
Motions of sprites 1 and 0 that $9517 starts.
Motions of sprites 4 and 3 that $9577 starts.
Pointers to the joystick direction list of each facing ($91,x).
9 joystick directions: none, forward, back, down, up, down-forward, up-forward, down-back, up-back. $84e9 finds the index.
The same list for facing 1: left and right are swapped.
Move selection row of each move number when fire is not pressed.
Move selection row of each move number when fire is pressed.
Move selection rows, 9 bytes each (12 rows): the next move for each direction index of joystick_dirs. $84f7 reads row n at $ccd0+9n.
Bit n for index n (8 bytes): sprite bits, voice bits and distance bits.
All bits except bit n for index n (8 bytes).
Address of each of the 9 sprite parts in the fighter buffer at $05ca. The buffer has 3 x 3 parts, 9 bytes for each line.
Offset in the fighter buffer of each of the 63 bytes of a sprite part.
Offset in the work bitmap of each byte of a fighter buffer line, from the last byte to the first. Each byte fills one cell column.
Offset of character rows 0-7 in the work bitmap (320 bytes each).
Nothing reads these bytes. They hold the $00/$ff fill pattern of RAM after power-on. The Hotline trainer puts its code at $ce00-$ce0b.

Bitmap of the arena that is not on screen: character rows 7-22, columns 4-35, 256 bytes for each row. Part 1 has another picture here than part 2. $8ddd swaps it with $a50e-$b50d when the arena changes. The code sets $01 to $20 to read it.
Screen RAM of the arena that is not on screen, 40 bytes for each row. The bytes differ from part 2. $8e06 swaps rows 7-22, columns 4-35 with $4400. Nothing reads the other bytes of $e000-$e3ff.
24 bytes after the 1000 screen bytes of the stored arena. Nothing reads them.
24 bytes after the 1000 screen bytes of the stored arena. They are the same as $47e8-$47ff: the stored arena is a copy of all 1 KB of the screen. Nothing reads them.
Colour RAM of the arena that is not on screen. The bytes differ from part 2. $8e06 swaps rows 7-22, columns 4-35 with $d800. Nothing reads the other bytes of $e400-$e7ff.
24 bytes after the 1000 colour bytes of the stored arena. Nothing reads them.

24 bytes after the 1000 colour bytes of the stored arena. Nothing reads them. As in $e400-$e7e7, the low nibbles are colours and the high nibbles are irregular, as a CPU read of the colour RAM $d800-$dbff gives.
Font of the text printer, 8 bytes for each glyph (39 glyphs): space, A-Z, 0-9, "(" and ")". $9215 gives the glyph address $e800+8n. $9173 makes multicolour cells from each glyph.
72 zero bytes after the font. Nothing reads them.
8 frames of the corner animations, 4 x 4 cells each (128 bytes), cell by cell and row by row. $e980-$eb7f are the right corner frames, $eb80-$ed7f the left corner frames.
Tune data of tunes $00-$56, in the RAM under the KERNAL ROM. The format is the same as at $a0eb.
Nothing reads these bytes. They hold the $00/$ff fill pattern of RAM after power-on.

13 sprites of the end of the story of part 2. $8c70 swaps them with the sprites at $54c0-$57ff (pointers $53-$5f). Only quit_to_demo calls $8c70, when $bb bit 7 is set. Part 1 never sets it, so nothing reads these sprites.
Nothing reads $ff80-$fff9. $ff80-$ffef hold the $00/$ff fill pattern of RAM after power-on.
The same 10 bytes as $9ff0-$9ff9 (the end of filter_setting_0d and the start of filter_setting_0e).
$fff0-$fffe hold the same bytes as $9ff0-$9ffe (the end of filter_setting_0d to the start of filter_setting_0f). $ffff repeats $fffe.
NMI vector. The start at $8009 writes $93af (an RTI) here.
Reset vector RAM. The program does not use it.
IRQ vector. The start at $8009 writes $937e (the IRQ handler) here.
